extracted.intended_audience: citizens and voters of New York; delegates and readers engaged in the 1787 Constitutional debate
extracted.subtask_description: Comparative analysis of historical confederacies (Germanic empire, United Netherlands, Swiss cantons, Poland, Achaean league) to identify structural defects of confederations and to argue for a stronger national government with enforcement and revenue powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereignty over sovereigns (government over governments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental principle on which [some confederacies] rests, that the empire is a community of sovereigns, that the diet is a representation of sovereigns and that the laws are addressed to sovereigns, renders the empire a nerveless body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'sovereignty over sovereigns' is described as 'a solecism in theory' and in practice 'subversive of the order and ends of civil polity, by substituting VIOLENCE in place of LAW.' Effective government should legislate for individuals and possess means of peaceful coercion (the magistry) rather than rely on force against sovereign members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction to federal laws / enforcement capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The total want of a SANCTION to its laws: The United States, as now composed, have no powers to exact obedience, or punish disobedience to their resolutions, either by pecuniary mulcts, by a suspension or divestiture of privileges, or by any other constitutional mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A confederacy must be able to enforce its laws; otherwise it is 'a government destitute even of the shadow of constitutional power to enforce the execution of its own laws.' Lack of explicit constitutional enforcement powers produces helplessness when members disobey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual guaranty of state governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The want of a mutual guaranty of the State governments is another capital imperfection in the federal plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national guaranty is needed to protect against domestic usurpations and violent overturns of state constitutions. This guaranty should not prevent lawful, peaceable reforms by a state's people; it should operate only against changes effected by violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability of national government to raise own revenues (vs quotas)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of regulating the contributions of the States to the common treasury by QUOTAS is another fundamental error in the Confederation... There can be no common measure of national wealth, and, of course, no general or stationary rule by which the ability of a state to pay taxes can be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorize the national government to raise revenues directly (imposts, excises) rather than depend on requisitioned quotas. Taxes on articles of consumption self-limit (reduce consumption if excessive) and over time find an equilibrium, avoiding the glaring inequalities and oppression created by quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impracticability of unanimity for important decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In all important cases, not only the provinces but the cities must be unanimous... In critical emergencies, the States-General are often compelled to overleap their constitutional bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of unanimity delay action (treaties, military preparations), force constitutional usurpations in emergencies, or produce paralysis. A useful federal design must avoid unanimity rules that cripple timely responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective federal military (small, poorly maintained, locally biased)
rubrics_metrics.description: The small body of national troops... is defectively kept up, badly paid, infected with local prejudices, and supported by irregular and disproportionate contributions to the treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A federal defense requires reliable standing forces properly funded and insulated from local prejudices; ad hoc or uneven contributions produce ineffective military preparedness and slow mobilization in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability to foreign intrigue and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Romans... seduced the members from the league... foreign nations have long considered themselves as interested in the changes made by events in this constitution; and have, on various occasions, betrayed their policy of perpetuating its anarchy and weakness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal dissension and constitutional weakness invite foreign manipulation. A durable union must limit opportunities for external powers to play members against one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws addressed to sovereigns rather than individuals are ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental principle... that the laws are addressed to sovereigns, renders the empire a nerveless body, incapable of regulating its own members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal legislation must be framed and enforced in a manner that applies to political communities and individuals in a way that produces compliance — addressing sovereigns alone leaves enforcement to their will and produces impotence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency to private wars and oppression among member states
rubrics_metrics.description: The history of Germany is a history of wars between the emperor and the princes and states; of wars among the princes and states themselves; of the licentiousness of the strong, and the oppression of the weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A confederation that cannot prevent or adjudicate internal conflicts will suffer civil devastation; the union must have mechanisms to restrain member-on-member aggression and protect weaker parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure of intermediate structures (circles/districts) to execute commands
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiment of dividing the empire into nine or ten circles... Each circle is the miniature picture of the deformities of this political monster. They either fail to execute their commissions, or they do it with all the devastation and carnage of civil war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating intermediate jurisdictions to delegate coercion often reproduces the federal constitution's defects at a smaller scale; such schemes can either fail to act or act destructively. Design must avoid ineffective or violent local enforcement proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of common federal institutions (treasury, troops, coin, judicatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: They [Swiss cantons] have no common treasury; no common troops even in war; no common coin; no common judicatory; nor any other common mark of sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A union lacking basic common institutions cannot function as a true nation; survival depends on peculiar local factors (topography, weakness) rather than constitutional strength — such arrangements are poor models for a durable federal government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unequal capacities and the problem of single dominant or many-equal members
rubrics_metrics.description: It has more than once happened, that the deficiencies had to be ultimately collected at the point of the bayonet; a thing practicable, though dreadful, in a confederacy where one of the members exceeds in force all the rest, and where several of them are too small to meditate resistance; but utterly impracticable in one composed of members, several of which are equal to each other in strength and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal design must account for disparities among members: if one dominates, coercive collection is possible but dangerous; if many are equal, coercion becomes impracticable. Equitable, effective mechanisms for raising resources and enforcing obligations are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parochial pride and repellant quality of sovereignty impede consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: The repellant quality, incident to the nature of sovereignty, and which time continually strengthens, prevents any reform whatever, founded on a proper consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional arrangements must overcome the natural resistance of sovereign members to cede powers; otherwise, necessary consolidation and reform will be blocked and the union will remain feeble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotas produce glaring inequality due to lack of common wealth metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the value of lands, nor the numbers of the people... has any pretension to being a just representative. The attempt... to regulate the contributions of the members of a confederacy by any such rule, cannot fail to be productive of glaring inequality and extreme oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fixed quotas based on inadequate proxies (land, population); instead enable national revenue mechanisms that better reflect ability to pay and that equilibrate burdens across time and objects of taxation.
